top_news.title: Is MoE Routing a Huffman Code? Discovering the Frequency-Diversity Law in Chain-of-Thought
top_news.dek: Researchers identify that MoE routing functions as a Huffman code, optimizing expert allocation based on token frequency and task complexity.
top_news.brief: A new study reveals that Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routing is not just a selection mechanism but an information-theoretic process. By applying the 'Frequency-Diversity Law,' the authors show that models like Phi-3.5-MoE and Gemma-4-27B-A4B dynamically route common tokens to sparse experts while reserving diverse expert committees for rare, complex tasks.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram illustrating MoE routing as a Huffman coding tree

top_news.title: Show HN: OneCLI – OSS credential gateway that keeps secrets out of AI agents
top_news.dek: OneCLI is an open-source credential gateway that prevents secret leakage by injecting API keys into AI agents at runtime.
top_news.brief: OneCLI acts as a secure intermediary between AI agents and external services. Instead of hardcoding credentials into agent configurations, developers store them in a centralized vault. The gateway then transparently injects the necessary keys during execution, ensuring agents never directly access or store sensitive secrets.
top_news.image_alt: OneCLI architecture diagram showing secret injection flow

top_news.title: Team uses AlphaFold AI to redesign gene-editing proteins to make them safer
top_news.dek: Researchers are using AlphaFold to redesign gene-editing proteins to minimize off-target DNA modifications.
top_news.brief: Gene-editing therapies face safety challenges due to off-target effects, where proteins edit unintended DNA sequences. By leveraging AlphaFold to identify the structural components responsible for these errors, scientists aim to engineer more precise proteins that improve the safety profile of genomic interventions.

top_news.title: Anthropic: Project Pilot: Can AI models fly drones?
top_news.dek: Anthropic and Andon Labs introduced Drone-Bench to evaluate AI model performance in autonomous drone navigation.
top_news.brief: The benchmark tests whether AI models can autonomously pilot drones to locate and track individuals. This research is part of a broader effort to understand how frontier models interact with the physical world, following previous experiments with robotic shop management and navigation.
top_news.image_alt: Drone flying in a test environment

top_news.title: Kimi K3 vs Claude Fable 5 on DeepSWE: Cost and Coding
top_news.dek: A performance comparison of Kimi K3 and Claude Fable 5 on the DeepSWE benchmark highlights trade-offs between accuracy and cost.
top_news.brief: Testing across 452 DeepSWE rollouts shows Claude Fable 5 leading in pass@1 accuracy by 1.4 points. However, Kimi K3 outperforms in pass@4 scenarios and offers 2.8x higher efficiency in terms of successful solves per dollar spent.
top_news.image_alt: Bar chart comparing AI model coding performance and cost

primary.title: Meet Gigatoken: A Rust BPE Tokenizer that Encodes Text at 24.53 GB/s, up to 989x Faster than HuggingFace Tokenizers
primary.summary: Gigatoken is an MIT-licensed Rust BPE tokenizer that encodes text at gigabytes per second. On a 144-core AMD EPYC 9565, it runs GPT-2 tokenization at 24.53 GB/s. That is 989x HuggingFace tokenizers and 681x tiktoken, against baselines already written in multithreaded Rust. The gains come from a hand-written SWAR pretokenizer and pretoken caching, not a faster BPE merge loop.
